big_case_rationale: Nationally watched election-law fight over documentary proof of citizenship and the NVRA's 90-day quiet period, RNC against the DNC and voting-rights groups with the United States in support, decided ahead of the 2028 cycle.

semantic_claims.proposition: The majority rules for the RNC on statutory-text grounds that confine the NVRA to its enumerated subjects: Arizona v. Inter Tribal Council's 'accept and use' holding governs only the federal form, so nothing in 52 U.S.C. §§20505-20508 bars Arizona from demanding documentary proof of citizenship from state-form applicants; the §20507(c)(2) 90-day quiet period governs systematic removal of registrants who became ineligible, not persons — noncitizens — who were never eligible to register at all; and the 2018 LULAC consent decree cannot permanently disable the Arizona Legislature's authority over election rules, adopting the Eighth Circuit's Carson v. Simon view. The constitutional backdrop — the States' power to enforce voter qualifications — is invoked as confirmation, not as the holding's basis.

The stated ground is categorical rather than Arizona-bound: the majority announces rules good for every State — that the NVRA leaves States free to require documentary proof of citizenship on their own state registration forms, and that the 90-day provision never blocks removal programs aimed at noncitizen registrants — rather than resting on the LULAC decree's particular terms, Arizona's enforcement record, or a fact-specific remand. It stops short of the federal-form and mail-voting questions, which sit outside the granted questions presented.
